messages:
Alice (Prod): Heads-up — ACME launched a routing/response-quality toggle this morning. Several mid-market customers pinged Sales asking for the same. I want to propose a short playbook: how we translate customer signal -> roadmap request -> launch guardrails.
Ben (PM): Can you paste the customer asks? Are they asking for parity (same UX) or just outcome parity (lower latency / more deterministic replies)?
Matt (Sales): Mostly outcome parity. Quotes: "give us a knob to prefer faster, cheaper responses for lower-risk flows" and "we need predictable costs for scaled tenants". One customer also asked about a fallback to a smaller model on spike.
Clara (Eng): Important to separate two things: 1) routing/cost toggles + 2) deterministic quality tiers. Implementing a toggle is fast; guaranteeing quality tiers requires evals and monitoring.
Sasha (Design): UX note — toggles must have clear labels and a short explanation tooltip. Customers will misinterpret "fast" vs "cheap". Proposed label: "Performance mode (lower latency, lower cost)" and a "Quality SLA" selector.
Dan (Solutions): For customers asking now, we can offer a Managed Config in Dedicated with a simple routing policy: route non-sensitive traffic to a quantized variant. That avoids a full product ship.
Ben (PM): I propose the playbook steps: 1) Triage signal (outcome vs UI) 2) Quick win checkbox (config + docs) 3) Eval set creation (customer-driven prompts) 4) Quality SLO definition 5) Launch gating + telemetry. Thoughts?
Clara (Eng): Add engineering gating: perf baseline, regression threshold (p99 latency <= X, cost delta <= Y%), and rollback conditions. Also require a canary on <5% traffic for 72h with live evals.
Alice (Prod): Agree. Also call out acceptance criteria for parity requests: must have an eval pass (no more than N% degrade on customer prompts) and an ops runbook for fallback routing.
Matt (Sales): Timeline pressure — customers expect something in 3 weeks. Can we hit a docs + Managed Config approach in that time?
Dan (Solutions): Yes for Managed Config + docs + a recommended model variant. Not for full console UX + rollout controls.
Sasha (Design): I can draft the tooltip and config panel mock by EOW if we aim for docs-first delivery.
Ben (PM): Ok plan: week 1: Managed Config prototype + docs + rollback runbook. Week 2: internal evals with customer prompt set + canary infra. Week 3: ship Managed Config + docs + canary and iterate. If metrics look good, schedule console toggle in Q next.
Clara (Eng): Heads-up on infra: we need quick routing rule support and a quantized model ready in the model catalog. I'll scope effort: estimate 5 engineer-days for rule plumbing + 3 days to validate model variant across seq lengths.
Alice (Prod): Risk log: potential quality complaints, support load during canary, and billing disputes if cost estimates mismatch. Add a clear billing note in the docs and pre-authorize support runbook.
Ben (PM): I'll own the playbook doc. Action items: Alice to own customer comms, Clara to scope infra, Sasha to mock, Dan to prepare Managed Config template, Matt to line up pilot customers. I'll assemble the eval prompts from the customers Matt lists.
rollout-bot: Canary created for project "acme-routing-knob" at 1768888905 — 2% traffic to quantized-variant.
Alice (Prod): Great. Let's reconvene on Thursday for a quick status sync. If anyone hits blockers, ping #eng-oncall for the routing infra. :thumbsup:
